findings.title: A link hit during a word read tears the card word (a hit can only clear bits): the marker takes a flood trunk as a caller, the unit drops the seizure and re-takes it mid-digit, or forwards it back the way it came
findings.mechanism: baseband_card.v:157 (local_trunk.v:192 the same) gates the word pin with the raw link_up of baseband_card.v:109, which drops after 47 us of silence on the far clock. word_rx.v:105-123 takes the eight frames after the select with no check, so a hit inside the window clears the bits whose frames it covers. (a) mini_marker.v:365 takes any word that is neither 11010 nor all zeros as a caller (S_TAKE, then the register and dial tone at 383-391). (b) net_unit.v:572-574 drops any non-trunk word, and st has already been set by cls_seen (570). st is cleared only by an M-low sample (566-567), which is the first dial break, and the make after that break is classified as a fresh seizure (283-284). (c) A hit over the frames of bits 6-7 leaves is_trunk true, and cls_dir = rd_word[7:6] (573) gives fwd_mask (505, 616-618) the wrong direction.
findings.trigger: A far-clock (fifth conductor) outage of 47 us to a few ms that overlaps the ~125 us of /HW frames after the first select of a fresh seizure. The unit's classifier and an idle marker select the same bit-time, so one hit tears both reads. Benches at real timers: tb_cls2 sc2 (marker idle), sc3 (register busy, so only the unit reads), tb_cls3 sc8 (a hit over bits 6-7 only).
findings.consequence: (a) sc2: a far caller dialling 3 2 2 1 is given THIS exchange's register and connected to local 32 ('1137.424 MK CONNECT caller 10 called 32'). This is a wrong number the caller cannot see. (b) sc3: the make after the first break is taken as a fresh seizure, the cell counts e=2 for a dialled 3 and claims, and 21 rings. (c) sc8: 'FWD 10 -> ok 1110 cand 00 30 40 11'. The flood goes back west on 11, so the W neighbour gets its own flood back two hops late (a late copy in the C05 sense), and north is never flooded.
findings.realistic: Survives real timing: all three were reproduced at real timers. It needs a hit that overlaps one ~0.13 ms window per seizure, which is about hit rate x (hit length + 0.1 ms) per classification. That is nil on a healthy link and ~1e-3 per seizure on a link taking ~10 hits/s, where C07's pulses dominate anyway. It is not a load effect.
findings.evidence: work/audit/cls/run_r2_sc2.log: '22.130 select of 10 (unit 1 marker 1): glitching its link', '22.264 cls read 10 word 01001000 trunk 0', '23.146 MK register -> 10', '1137.424 MK CONNECT caller 10 called 32', FAIL. run_r2_sc3.log: '632.262 cls read 10 word 01001000 trunk 0', '817.144 cls_seen 10', 'mon0 10 digit 2 (as e)', '1746.001 CLAIM 10', '21 ringing: hi 600', FAIL. run_c3_sc8.log: '22.264 cls read 10 word 00001011 trunk 1', 'HOLD 10 dir 0', '33.005 FWD 10 -> ok 1110 cand 00 30 40 11', 'W 11 a_out 1, N 71 a_out 0', FAIL. All PASS with fix2: run_f4_c2_sc2.log and run_f4_c2_sc3.log (the 01001000 read is re-read as 11001011; HOLD at +3.2 ms), run_f4_c3_sc8.log (00001011 then 11001011 disagree, re-read, HOLD dir 3, legs N S E).
findings.fix: Best fix, at the card: hold the WORD through a hit exactly as C07's card fix holds A, by gating word_n with the card's poison/ride-through latch instead of the raw link_up. It costs 0 parts beyond C07's ~1 package per card and protects every reader (unit, marker, sweep). Reader-side alternative, tested in work/audit/cls/fix2: the unit reads the word twice a pass apart and acts only when the two agree, with one re-read of a word that is neither a trunk nor a caller class (a '574, a '688 and gates; +~1 ms per hop). The marker takes as a caller only a line (xxxx1111) or a tone trunk (11011). A hit only clears bits, so it cannot forge either (a few gates). Caveat: port-form words (answers-to, call nail) would then be refused as callers; that is fine in top_net today.

findings.title: `mine` does not cover the sweep's candidates, and C_ACT and C_UNHOLD write cls_port without checking it again: a short far seizure on the origin's candidate makes the classifier hold, then free, the trunk the origin has just seized
findings.mechanism: net_unit.v:429-438: mine covers the N_SEIZE o_cand, d_held, the F_WRITE f_cand and rs_held, and nothing while the sweep runs (N_HUNT, F_HUNT: h_cand). cls_seen (283-284) tests mine only at its own sample. The read then takes at least 1.1 ms (C_WAIT behind a sweep read, 292 and 553-555), and C_ACT (595-611) pushes the HOLD without looking again. The C_HOLD watch (584-588) and C_UNHOLD (590-594) then push the port free, also unchecked. The sweep's CONFIRM (779-785) passes the port if the far M has fallen and the classifier's HOLD is not yet visible at the port's turn.
findings.trigger: A far seizure on this exchange's origin (or forward) candidate that rises after the sweep has read the port and ends before the port's CONFIRM turn. Reproduced with tb_cls2 sc4 at real timers: a 0.77 ms blip on N trunk 71 during the origin sweep's last read. Short far seizures come from far glare resolution (a far origin that takes glare as its claim drops its other directions within ~2 ms; C03's trigger list), a far f_cancel, or a bounce.
findings.consequence: In run_r2_sc4.log the origin's N_SEIZE of 71 (to caller 20) is pushed first. The classifier's HOLD of 71 (to 00, BUSY) follows; it prints 'mine 0 nst 4' because mine is computed for sp_port, not cls_port. Then its UNHOLD writes 71 free while the origin holds it. The caller silently loses that direction. When the far end later seizes 71 as free for a flood of its own, the origin takes that M as the claim, and caller 20 is joined to a stranger. The hold also gives the blip a monitor cell (C03's stale cell).
findings.realistic: Survives real timing: reproduced at real timers. It needs a ~1-3 ms far seizure on the one channel that is the current candidate, inside a ~10 ms sweep. When a link's two ends are strapped to hunt in opposite order, the far end reaches that channel only when it is the last one free. Very rare, but it is the worst kind of failure: two callers joined, silently.
findings.evidence: work/audit/cls/run_r2_sc4.log: '227.873 sweep's last read in flight (h_idx 70, scan 67): far blip on 71', '227.911 cls_seen 71 (cst 0, rd_free 0)', '228.645 blip over', '229.029 HOLD 71 dir 0 mine 0 nst 4', '229.911 UNHOLD 71 nst 4 d_held 1111', '71 latch -> 00 bsy 0', 'FAIL sc4: a trunk the origin holds listens to its caller', '755.003 origin claimed 1 trunk 71', '20 hears ones 1 zeros 0; 20's latch -> 71', FAIL. With fix2, run_f4_c2_sc4.log PASS ('71 latch -> 20 bsy 1', 'origin claimed 0').
findings.fix: Look at the port again before writing: hold only if cls_port shows M, not BUSY and not `mine` at a later turn. fix2 does this at the second read's select, with no parts beyond the double read. A zero-latency form samples M/BUSY/mine at the read's own select turn, as the sweep does with h_m/h_b (two flip-flops). Also never UNHOLD a port that is `mine` at the watch's sample: net_unit.v:586 'cst <= mine ? C_IDLE : C_UNHOLD' is one gate, because mine is already computed for sp_port == cls_port there. Alternative: OR h_cand into mine while hst != H_IDLE (four more '688s).

findings.title: The dealt-with bit st is cleared by any M-low sample, so on an unheld trunk the make after a dial break is taken as a fresh seizure, mid-number
findings.mechanism: net_unit.v:566-567 clears st on every sample with M low. port.v:147 shows BUSY during a dial break of an armed port only through (fm && !m), which 568 ignores because it sets st only with M up. Take an unheld trunk under a far caller: one the classifier has not reached yet, one it dropped, or one released under a standing M. The first break of a digit clears its st, and at the make it is M . /BUSY . /st. That is cls_seen (283-284), so it gets a hold, a monitor cell (612-615) and a forward (616-621) from mid-digit.
findings.trigger: New triggers: (i) the called party hangs up first, the trunk port releases under the far caller's standing M, and the far caller then dials on (tb_cls2 sc6); (ii) a trunk whose first word read was torn (word-read-across-link-hit, sc3). Known triggers with the same root: a seizure still waiting for a busy classifier at its first break (C05), the C_HOLD watch's unhold (C04), and an LTU link returning under a standing M (C07 link-return-fresh-seizure).
findings.consequence: sc6 on the snapshot: after the release, '3205.137 cls_seen 10', then 'mon0 10 digit 2 (as e)' and '4133.995 CLAIM 10'. That is a claim on a truncated count; the far caller dialled 3 2 2 1. Spec: exchange/network.md 3.3 says 'a trunk whose BUSY falls under a standing M is no fresh seizure', and 3.4 rule 1 says 'the classifier takes a port only on a rise its bit has seen'. Neither holds once the far caller dials.
findings.realistic: Survives real timing: sc6 and sc3 were reproduced at real timers. Trigger (i) needs the far caller to dial inside the window where this port has released but the far M still stands. In a pure pulse-flood network both ends release on the same T_REL, so that window is ~1-2 ms plus RC tolerance, which is rare; it is wider behind a carrier or far end that holds A. Trigger (ii) is rare because hits are rare. The C05 route needs a burst (see classifier-scan-order-priority).
findings.evidence: work/audit/cls/run_o6_sc6.log: '3144.996 10 latch -> 00 bsy 0 busy 0, far M still up; st[10] 1', '3205.137 cls_seen 10', '4133.995 CLAIM 10', 'claims 1 more'. run_r2_sc3.log (see word-read-across-link-hit). With fix2's rule: run_f4_c2_sc6.log 'classified 0 more times, claims 0 more', PASS. In run_f4_c2_sc1K8.log, 17, still waiting at its first break, is never taken (a lost copy), and 16 is not re-classified after its watch unholds. In run_f4_c3_sc7.log the overtaken 47 is never taken and there is no claim.
findings.fix: BUSY first: 'if (sp_busy) st <= 1; else if (!sp_m) st <= 0;'. This is 0 gates, a rewiring at the input of the '164 chain. A port seen BUSY (a dial break of an armed port, or an LTU's MUTE_BLK) stays dealt with until M and BUSY are both down, so a make after a break is never a fresh seizure. A copy the classifier had not reached before its first break becomes a LOST copy: never held and never forwarded mid-digit, which is safe (rule 1). Cost: that copy stays unheld under M, and the marker's C16 re-read loop runs on it for the rest of the call (run_f4_c2_sc1K8.log: 1334 reads of 16 in 3 s, and 17 hidden behind it). Regressed with the rest of fix2: tb_net 87/88 (the one failure is the intended blip change), tb_lfull 40/40, tb_chain 32/32.

findings.title: After every hold watch the classifier starts again at port 00, so waiting seizures are taken lowest-numbered first, not oldest first: a high-numbered trunk can be overtaken without bound and picked up after its first break
findings.mechanism: net_unit.v:584-587: C_HOLD counts cls_ms on tick_1k (frame_stb at scan 00, line 159) and leaves on the tick where cls_ms passes T_ARM+1, i.e. at scan ~00. cls_seen (283-284) then takes the first M./BUSY./st port in scan order. A waiting seizure keeps st clear and is offered again only in scan order, so every seizure that arrives on a lower-numbered port during a watch is served first. The C05 cluster has the 19 ms per seizure; this finding is about the order.
findings.trigger: tb_cls3 sc7 (snapshot, NMON=NRES=8, real timers): E trunk 47 is seized 5 ms after W 10, and W 11-16 are seized at +10, +25, +45, +65, +85 and +105 ms. 47's far caller dials 3 2 2 1 with its first break 128 ms after its rise.
findings.consequence: 47 is held after all six later W seizures, whose holds are 19 ms apart. When the classifier comes free (~+155 ms) 47 is in its first break, so it is taken at the make: seen at +188.6 ms, cell armed 'AFTER THE FIRST BREAK', e counted 2 for a dialled 3, 'WRONG CLAIM on 47'. FIFO order would have held it at ~+20 ms. Under offered overload the order shows statistically: rise-to-hold max 18.3 ms on W (ports 10-17) against 38.7 ms on E (40-47), and all six waits over 19 ms were on E. With arrivals on lower ports faster than one per 19 ms, a high port waits indefinitely.
findings.realistic: Survives real timing: reproduced at real timers. It needs a burst faster than one seizure per 19 ms at one exchange (seven in 105 ms here). At monitor.md's reference loads the classifier is 0.4-7% busy and P(two or more seizures ahead) is 1e-5 to 5e-3 (an_model.out). In the overload run it was ~21% busy, the backlog never exceeded 2 and nothing was picked up late. It bites at a hub, in link-return storms and in ring laps (C19). It also makes network.md 3.4's 'up to 20 ms behind a classifier busy with an earlier hold' false.
findings.evidence: work/audit/cls/run_c3_sc7.log: '26.004 far seizure on 47', the holds of 11-16 at 41.280, 60.295, 79.311, 98.326, 117.342 and 136.357, '215.748 cls read 47', '216.630 mon7 arm 47 AFTER THE FIRST BREAK', '1143.002 WRONG CLAIM on 47: far caller dialled 3 2', '47: rise 26.0 seen +188.6 hold +189.7 cell +190.6 (first break at +128.0) e counted 2 claims 1'. work/audit/cls/an_c3_ovl.txt and an_f4_ovl.txt give rise-to-hold by group. With fix2, 47 becomes a lost copy with no claim (run_f4_c3_sc7.log).
findings.fix: Safety: the BUSY-first rule of st-cleared-by-dial-break (0 gates), so a copy not taken before its first break is never taken. Order: end the watch at the held port's own turn ('sp_fresh && sp_port == cls_port && cls_ms > T_ARM+1', reusing the '688 already there), so the classifier resumes after cls_port. That is round-robin: each waiting port is overtaken at most once per cycle, for 0 parts. True FIFO needs a small rise queue (~5 packages; the round-1 fix/). For the latency itself, see C05's 'take the watch off the classifier'.

findings.title: The mini marker connects a caller to a trunk port whose link is down (its word reads NONE), and the caller's dial pulses go out on the link when it returns
findings.mechanism: mini_marker.v:366 refuses a called port only when its word is a flood trunk. A trunk card with its link down reads 00000000 (baseband_card.v:157, local_trunk.v:192), so S_PROBE (474-491) sees M and BUSY clear and writes the connection both ways. extensions.md 2.2 says an OOS/none port 'gets cannot-complete', and mini-marker.md 8 says a trunk is 'never dialled: cannot-complete'.
findings.trigger: tb_cls2 sc5 at real timers: S trunk 30's far clock is stopped, 22 dials 3 0, the link returns, and 22 dials 2 1.
findings.consequence: '1824.509 MK read 30 word 00000000 ( called)', then '1825.391 MK CONNECT caller 22 called 30'. When the link returns the neighbour sees 22's M as a seizure, and 3 breaks go out while 22 dials 2 1. That is a flood seizure with no key, no origin guard and no T_CLAIM, which the neighbour holds, monitors and forwards.
findings.realistic: Survives real timing: reproduced at real timers. It needs a caller to dial the h s of a trunk channel on any highway but 1 while its link is down, i.e. a misdial during an outage. Rare.
findings.evidence: work/audit/cls/run_r2_sc5.log: the lines above, 'FAIL sc5: a trunk port is never connected to a dialling line', and 'breaks sent on 30's link while 22 dialled 2 1: 3'. With fix2, run_f4_c2_sc5.log PASS ('22 latch -> 03', 0 breaks).
findings.fix: Refuse a called port whose word is not a line (fix2: !rd_line, a few gates). At minimum, refuse one that reads NONE by testing (rd_trunk || rd_word == 0) at :366 as :365 already does; the zero detect exists, so this is 0 parts.

findings.title: A sub-HIT dip of M inside the C_HOLD watch unholds a live seizure; it is re-held with a second cell, both cells claim the same call, and the refusal of the second claim points the taken call at cannot-complete
findings.mechanism: net_unit.v:586 treats any M-low sample in the watch as a death (C04's mechanism). 590-594 write the hold away and cancel the forward but keep the cell (C03). The M-low sample cleared st (567), so the port is re-classified (283-284) with a second cell (612-615). The dip is shorter than HIT, so both cells count the same digits and reach M_DONE on the same tick (641). w_claim serves them one after the other (487, 656-671). The second att finds the register attached and is refused (mini_marker.v:282, 320-327), so the trunk is written to NOGO with BUSY and CLAIM.
findings.trigger: tb_cls3 sc11 (snapshot, real timers): a 3 ms far-M dip (a link hit) 8 ms after the rise, after which the far caller dials 2 2 2 1.
findings.consequence: The log shows '29.146 UNHOLD 10 far alive 1', '32.146 RECLASS 10', a second HOLD and mon1, '1038.003 CLAIM 10', '1038.695 CLAIM 10' and '1038.985 MK refuses the claim on 10'. The far caller hears cannot-complete from b until the connect after s re-points the trunk (~1.7 s), and a caller who believes it hangs up. The forward is cancelled and issued again. Had its legs already been written, R_GONE would drop them and the re-forward would re-take the lowest free channel 10-15 ms later. That is a break >= HIT at every downstream cell, C03's re-seize route (reasoning, not run).
findings.realistic: Survives real timing: reproduced at real timers. It needs a sub-HIT M dip that straddles a port sample in the ~18 ms after a hold, i.e. link hits (C07 link-hit-extra-pulse). Rare. This confirms the origin audit's speculative cross-slice item.
findings.evidence: work/audit/cls/run_c3_sc11.log: the lines above and '10: held 2 times, unheld 1, cells 2, claims 2; refusals 1; 10 latch -> 21; 21 rung 1', FAIL. fix2 leaves it unchanged (run_f4_c3_sc11.log), as expected.
findings.fix: C04's fix closes it: M low in the watch must outlast a dial break before the unhold. The round-1 fix/ watchers (unhold only after CLR of low) also close it. Defence in depth: C03's fix (a) frees the cell at the unhold, which leaves one cell; or the claim handler ignores a second want on the port it has just claimed (one '688 against att_port).

findings.title: The sweep keeps one candidate per direction, so a far seizure of that channel between its read and its CONFIRM turn costs the whole direction though other trunks that way are free
findings.mechanism: net_unit.v:759-766 keeps one candidate per direction, and 779-782 clears h_ok[d] if that port shows M or BUSY at its confirm turn. Nothing hunts that direction again: 853-856 and 720-723 use h_ok as it stands.
findings.trigger: tb_cls3 sc9 (snapshot, real timers): 20 keys 1, and after the origin sweep has read W 10 free (h_idx 17) the far end seizes 10.
findings.consequence: 'origin nst 4 holds dirs 0111 ... W 11-17 busy 0000000': the call is flooded N, S and E only, and a destination reachable only westward gets cannot-complete after T_CLAIM. A forward loses the direction the same way.
findings.realistic: Real timers. When a link's two ends are strapped to hunt in opposite order (the glare bit at one end), the far end takes this end's lowest free channel only when it is the last free one, and then there is no second choice anyway, so there is no cost. It costs whenever both ends hunt the same way (glare strapped at neither end or at both), at about the far seizure rate on the link x the ~10 ms sweep.
findings.evidence: work/audit/cls/run_c3_sc9.log: '221.263 the sweep has read W 10 free: the far end seizes 10 (h_n 16)', '550.003 origin nst 4 holds dirs 0111 trunks N 71 S 30 E 40 ...; W 11-17 busy 0000000', FAIL. fix2 leaves it unchanged (run_f4_c3_sc9.log).
findings.fix: State in the trunk/network documents that the two ends of every link must strap opposite glare; then nothing is lost. If mis-strapping must be tolerated, keep the next-best candidate per direction (6 bits x 4, two '174s) and fall back to it at CONFIRM.

findings.title: Counted under load: residual glare on a forward's leg (C13) joined a stranger's seizure to a forward twice in 165 floods when the trunk groups were nearly full, and never at moderate load
findings.mechanism: net_unit.v:681-690: a resolver takes any M on a held leg as the claim (R_LEG) and writes the way back (691-708). This is C13's mechanism.
findings.trigger: c3_ovl: 30 floods/s offered on 16 trunks, with 61% of floods blocked at the far end. The bench's far end hunts highest-first against the unit's lowest-first, so the two ends meet on the last free channel.
findings.consequence: '672.238 RESOLVER 4 takes M on leg 3 as a claim (in 41)' and '13140.206 RESOLVER 3 takes M on leg 3 as a claim (in 42)': a forward is joined to the far end's own new seizure, and nothing counts it.
findings.realistic: Real timers. 2 in 165 floods (1.2%) with the groups nearly full; 0 in 101 floods at the r1 load (27% blocked) and 0 in 176 on fix2's overload run.
findings.evidence: work/audit/cls/run_c3_ovl.log (the lines above; SUMMARY 'resolver_leg_claims=2'), run_c3_r1.log ('resolver_leg_claims=0'), run_f4_c3_ovl.log ('resolver_leg_claims=0').

findings.title: Counted under load: the one register refused 2 of 5 incoming claims, and every dial-tone delay over 10 ms was the register held by another call (C15)
findings.mechanism: mini_marker.v:282 and 320-327 refuse a claim when the one register is busy (C15). A caller waits for dial tone while the register is in YIELD on a network call.
findings.trigger: c3_r1: 5 floods/s, 10% of them dialling this exchange (2 2 2 1), plus 4 phones making local and network calls.
findings.consequence: 5 claims: 3 attached and 2 refused ('15476.390 MK refuses the claim on 45', '31023.216 MK refuses the claim on 10'). Dial tone had p50 3 ms, but 1.39 s and 1.83 s when a network call held the register. In the overload runs one lift got no dial tone within 3 s: a later caller on a lower port took the register first (the known, accepted scan-order starvation of callers) and then held it on a network call.
findings.realistic: Real timers. Not caused by the read path: the marker's read wait was at most 9 ms in every run.
findings.evidence: work/audit/cls/run_c3_r1.log (LC lines, 'MK register' and 'MK refuses' lines, SUMMARY 'refusals=2'), an_c3_r1.txt; run_f4_c3_ovl.log ('LC p=32 t=10220.0 dt=-1.00', 'MK register -> 22' at 11317).

findings.title: Counted under load: the marker reads each waiting trunk ~0.5 times per flood, but an unheld trunk under M is read every 2 ms for the whole call and hides the 8 ports after it (C16)
findings.mechanism: mini_marker.v:337-345 and 365: any M./BUSY port is read, and a trunk goes straight back to S_IDLE with nothing remembered (C16).
findings.trigger: Load runs; a trunk left unheld under a standing far M: after a C04 unhold, a copy lost under the BUSY-first st rule, or a release under a standing M.
findings.consequence: Under Poisson load the marker read trunks 99 times for 165 floods (c3_ovl) and 42 times for 101 (c3_r1), and its read wait stayed at most 9 ms. With an unheld trunk under M it read 16 1334 times in 3 s (run_f4_c2_sc1K8.log), and 10 1331-1332 times in 3 s (run_f3_sc6.log, run_f4_c2_sc6.log). Port 17, just after 16, was never read, so a line there would get no dial tone for the duration.
findings.realistic: Real timers. Frequent but short in normal traffic. It lasts a whole call whenever a trunk is left unheld under M, which the BUSY-first st fix makes a deliberate outcome for late copies. So C16's fix (a read-once bit in the marker) should go with it.
findings.evidence: work/audit/cls/run_c3_ovl.log and run_c3_r1.log (SUMMARY mk_reads), run_f4_c2_sc1K8.log (16: 1334 reads, 333-3358 ms; 17: 0), run_f4_c2_sc6.log (1332).
findings.fix: C16's (a per-port read-once bit in the marker). It is needed more once late copies are left unheld by design.

findings.title: No tree bench tears a word, blips a sweep candidate, bursts low ports behind a high one, dips M inside the hold watch, releases a trunk under a standing M, or dials a trunk whose link is down
findings.mechanism: tb_net, tb_chain, tb_lnet, tb_lfull and tb_lchain are all green on the snapshot (work/base-*.log) while all seven defects above are present. tb_net 14 even asserts the behaviour fix2 removes: that a 0.9 ms blip IS held and given a monitor.
findings.consequence: Six wrong-number or stuck-direction paths in the read path ship untested.
findings.evidence: work/base-*.log all PASS. On the snapshot, work/audit/cls/tb_cls2.v (sc2-sc6) and tb_cls3.v (sc7, sc8, sc9, sc11) go red: run_r2_sc2..5.log, run_o6_sc6.log, run_c3_sc7/8/9/11.log. run_f4_tree_net.log fails only at tb_net 14's first check under fix2.
findings.fix: Adopt tb_cls2 sc2-6 and tb_cls3 sc7-9 and sc11 as one single-exchange bench at real timers (about 1-2 min wall each). Change tb_net 14 to check that the blip leaves 11 idle and no cell held, rather than that it was held. Add faults.py entries for the fixes: the BUSY-first st rule, the look-again, no UNHOLD on mine, and the called-port NONE refusal.

sound.claim: Two readers can never select different ports in one bit-time, and nobody selects while another read's word is on /HW
sound.why: word_rx.v:103 decides a select at the frame edge on SCAN == at and win == 0, and every reader's win counts every select seen on the shared /WS (105-117). Two selects in one bit-time therefore name the same port, and both take its word. The bench counter 'readers selecting different ports in one bit-time' was 0 in every round-1 and round-2 run.

sound.claim: The marker's word reads cannot be starved by back-to-back sweeps, and the classifier's reads cannot be starved by the marker
sound.why: During H_SWEEP the only select slots with win == 0 are the sweep's own selects. A pending marker read of that same port rides along and takes the same word, and H_CONFIRM issues no reads, so a marker read waits at most about one sweep. cls_issue outranks h_issue (net_unit.v:292, 453-454), and the marker's C16 loop selects at most every other pass. Measured at real timers: marker read issue-to-select mean 1.15-2.43 ms, max 8.99 ms over 261 reads; classifier read issue-to-select 0.93-0.99 ms over 638 reads (one turn, never more). Sweeps averaged 10.45-10.51 ms, max 11.74 ms, against ~10 ms nominal (runs c3_ovl, c3_r1, f4_c3_ovl).

sound.claim: A trunk's word cannot read as not-a-trunk at link-up, at power-up or across the '165 reload boundary
sound.why: M and the word pin are gated by the same term: baseband_card.v:154/157 (link_up && settled) and local_trunk.v:188/192 (live). The first read comes at least one turn after M rises, so it is always a whole word. The '165 is reloaded every octet from jumpers (baseband_card.v:144-145, local_trunk.v:179-180), so a read spanning two loads is consistent. Only a hit during the read tears it (word-read-across-link-hit).

sound.claim: The classifier's and the sweep's answers cannot be confused
sound.why: rd_free = !rd_busy && !rd_req (249), so only one owner issues at a time. rd_own is set at issue (551, 557), and the answer is routed by it (572, 757). The sweep keeps the M/BUSY sample of its own select turn, and a deferred select re-captures it (756).

sound.claim: A seizure that arrives while the classifier is busy is always picked up later, never lost, as long as it has had no dial break; every classifier state ends in bounded time
sound.why: A waiting seizure shows M with BUSY clear, so st is neither set (568) nor cleared, and cls_seen takes it at its first turn after C_IDLE. C_WAIT lasts at most one sweep read, C_READ one turn plus 8 frames, C_ACT and C_UNHOLD a queue drain, and C_HOLD T_ARM+2 ms. After every load drain nothing was held (c3_ovl, c3_r1, f4_c3_ovl: reg, marker, dirs, resolvers, monitors, hunt, cst, fst and nst all idle, no port BUSY). The mid-digit pickup after a break is the finding, not a loss.

sound.claim: The classifier is never the capacity limit
sound.why: At real timers it takes a trunk seizure every 19.0 ms (read ~1.1 ms plus C_HOLD; holds at +1.2, 20.3, 39.3 ms ... in run_r2_sc1.log), i.e. 53 per second, and a line lift costs one ~1.1 ms read. 16 channels at ~2 s per flood copy cannot offer more than ~8 per second. In the overload run the far end found no free trunk for 61% of the offered floods while the classifier was ~21% busy with a backlog of at most 2. At monitor.md's reference loads it is 0.4-7% busy (an_model.out).

sound.claim: No late pickup occurs under Poisson load at realistic occupancy
sound.why: Across 442 carried seizures in three load runs at real timers (c3_ovl, c3_r1, f4_c3_ovl), no cell armed after a first break, nothing was held twice and there was no wrong claim. That includes 84 far callers dialling one pulse above this exchange's code (3 2), 23 of them with the first break 60-200 ms after the rise. The classifier backlog never exceeded 2 and rise-to-hold never exceeded 41.7 ms. The late pickup needs a burst of ~6 seizures within ~100 ms at one exchange (sc7), or C05's late flood.

sound.claim: `mine` covers the interval from the confirm turn to the seize becoming visible, so true glare is never also classified as a seizure
sound.why: The confirm pass visits each port once in exactly 64 fresh samples. A far rise after a candidate's confirm turn is next sampled after h_done, when nst = N_SEIZE (o_ok) or fst = F_WRITE (f_ok) and then d_held or rs_held put it in mine (429-438). tb_lfull stayed green on fix2 (40/40). The gap is only before the confirm turn (the finding).

sound.claim: st never stays set while M is down
sound.why: Every M-low sample clears it (net_unit.v:566-567); under fix2's rule, every sample with M and BUSY both low does. It stays set for good only while M stands for good (a phantom, C08).

overload:
Overload is not graceful: past the knee the network collapses.

**The mechanism.** Each register is held for a network origin through all of 1 e b h s, and a refused call holds it just as long (net_unit.v:881, o_last). A claim that finds the register busy is refused at once (mini_marker.v:282). With traffic in both directions, each register sits in YIELD for its own outgoing caller when the other exchange's claim arrives. So as offered load rises, carried network traffic falls to zero while register occupancy goes to 1:
- scale 8, pnet 100%: 17.5 → 2.5 → 0 OK/min an exchange at 0.9, 1.8 and 3.2 attempts/s
- real timers: 1 call a minute at about 1000 attempts/h an exchange

**What the caller sees at overload.**
- No dial tone for 19-42% of callers at 2-4x the knee (the scale-8 timeout is 3 s, the real one 20 s).
- Dial tone goes to the lowest-numbered lines. Pooled over 16 runs, no dial tone for 0.4% of attempts from lines 20-37 and 27% from lines 50-77.
- Refused callers dial all five digits, then hear cannot-complete 20 ms after the last one (27 of 27 at i30k).
- At pnet 30%, local calls are still carried at the register's limit (72.5 a minute an exchange at i15k) while network calls die (1 of 22).
- Doomed calls keep holding trunks: at the collapse about 2.2 channels are busy while 0 or 1 calls are carried.

**Liveness is intact.**
- Every run drained to 26 of 26 invariants PASS, including 3-4x overload and the SCALE1 collapse: ports idle, register free, marker idle, origin, monitors, resolvers, sweep and unit idle, queues empty, no cable-B clash, no queue overflow, links up, phones quiet.
- No STUCK port, origin, monitor or att.
- The only STUCK lines were the marker_state watchdog (the marker never idle for 7.5 s at overload). Each ended by itself, with STUCK-END at 10.4-12.1 s.
- No state carries between calls, so recovery should be immediate once load falls. That rests on the model and the overload agent's step runs, not on runs here.

**What changes the collapse.**

findings.title: Two-way network traffic collapses: past about 0.75 attempts/s an exchange (scale 8), carried network calls fall towards zero instead of levelling off
findings.mechanism: Each exchange has one register. mini_marker.v:282 refuses at once any claim that finds r_busy set (outside S_WATCH), and mini_marker.v:273-274 takes a claim only when the register is free. Key 1 puts the register in S_YIELD (mini_marker.v:428-432) and keeps it there until u_done/u_nogo (mini_marker.v:496-520). The origin reaches N_DONE only at o_last, the caller's last digit (net_unit.v:410, :880-881). The origin also cannot tell a refusal from a take: the refusal's CLAIM raises M like a take (mini_marker.v:320-327, net_unit.v:795-798). So a doomed call holds its own register, its far trunk and its line for the whole 1 e b h s, as long as a call that succeeds. With traffic in both directions each register sits in YIELD for its own caller when the other exchange's claim arrives, and refuses it. Every refusal feeds the next.
findings.trigger: tb_load2 (A 2 2 and B 2 3 on the 8-channel local trunk, 48 lines each), pnet 100%, both exchanges originating, idle 60 s, 30 s or 15 s.

Register occupancy rises from .42 to .98 while the trunks stay at most 2.9 of 8 busy. Refused callers dial all five digits and then hear cannot-complete: postdial NOGO is 20 ms after the last digit, and none hear it earlier (27 of 27). The model (regmodel.py) peaks at 19.7 OK/min an exchange at 0.75 attempts/s with 55% refused. Nothing is stuck: 26 of 26 invariants pass after drain in every run.

**Method.** The study ran 16 RTL runs: 15 at scale 8 and 1 at SCALE1. Together they are 301 simulated s, 14 351 wall s and 625 calls. Every run passed its 26 invariants after drain.

**The model.** regmodel.py (NOT RTL) is a call-level model of the harness plus the RTL's register, claim and trunk rules. It reproduces every RTL point within binomial noise; the side-by-side is in rtl_vs_model.txt. capacity:
The limit is the one register an exchange, not the unit and not the trunks. Measured at scale 8 on tb_load2 (48 lines an exchange, pnet 50% both ways, NMON = NRES = 2):
- A local call holds the register 330-373 ms.
- A network call holds the ORIGIN register 730-760 ms whether it succeeds or not; it is held to o_last.
- A taken claim holds the far register about 410 ms.
- So the register saturates near 1.3 attempts/s/exchange; the knee is about 1.0 attempt/s/exchange.

Measured points (window by lift or alert time):
| load | offered, att/s/exch | reg_occ | net OK | connects/s (pair) | carried | source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.7x | 0.87 | .50/.53 | 7/14 | 1.21 | 2.03 E | smoke, work/load/smoke/load2_light.log |
| 1.6x | 1.78 | .91/.70 | 4/20 | 0.78 | 1.23 E | R2 |

- The network collapses long before the local side. Refusals follow the far register's occupancy (C15): 47% at 0.7x, 78% at 1.6x, 93-100% at 4x and above. Over all 23 runs: 298 claims, 15 taken, 283 refused.
- Transit resources did not run out on the chain at 4x, 10x or always-trying (r20-r22): at transit B nofwd 0, nomon 0, res_max 2 of 2. With one register (one origin bank) an exchange, at most one flood per neighbour is ever pending.
- A discrete-event model (overload/model.py) matches the RTL: 0.87 vs 0.85 att/s, reg .56 vs .50, net OK 49% vs 53% at 0.7x; 19.4 vs 18.9 att/s and 1% vs 0 success at always-trying.

Real time: dialling scales about 6.5-7x (pulses 5x, pause between digits 7.2x, pre-dial 8.3x).
- Model knee: about 0.15-0.3 attempts/s per 48-line exchange, i.e. 540-1100 attempts/h, or 11-23 attempts a line an hour.
- Model throughput peak: about 0.28 connected calls/s for the pair (~1000/h).
- Network completion is already only 50% at 0.15 att/s/exch (the harness default idle 300 s) and 10% at 0.3.
- SCALE1 check (r30), at 0.55 att/s/exch: reg_occ .93, dial tone mean 3.3 s and max 19.8 s (NODT at 20 s), 2 of 14 claims taken, 0.16 connects/s. A refused network attempt holds 4.7 s of register against 2.2 s for a local call.
- A normal busy hour (2-5 calls a line an hour) sits below the real knee, but C15 refusals are already 25-50% there.
overload:
Carried traffic does not hold at the knee. It collapses, first for the network and then for everything. The positive feedback is in the registers (C15), not in C14's unit pools, which never ran out.

tb_load2, scale 8 (connects by alert time):
| load | run | offered, att/s/exch | connects/s (pair) | carried | net OK | NODT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.7x | smoke | 0.87 | 1.21 | 2.03 E | 7/14 | 0 |
| 1.6x | R2 | 1.78 | 0.78 | 1.23 E | 4/20 | 31% |
| 4x | r3, 2-8 s | 5.58 | 1.17 | 1.35 E | 0/36 | 63% |
| 10x | r5, 1.5-6 s | 10.7 | 0.67 | 1.16 E | 0/50 | 77% |
| always-trying | R1 | 15.5-18.9 | 0 | 0 E | - | 85% |

At always-trying every called line is off hook waiting, so every served call is BUSY or refused.

The chain tb_load3:
- r20 (4x): 2.15 connects/s for 3 exchanges, network 0/61.
- r21 (10x): 0.44/s, network 0/137.
- r22 (always-trying): 0.

Why it collapses (regshare.py): the share of the origin register spent on network attempts that are then refused is 33% at 0.7x, 77% at 4x, 72% at 10x, 96% under a network jam, and 64% at real timers (r30). Each refused attempt costs twice a local call, and mutual refusal was seen live (r5 recovery: A64 and B34 each refused the other).

Recovery:
- Nothing is latched. The unit pools are idle at the next PROG, and all 23 runs pass their invariants.
- There is no queue, so the backlog of waiting lines is cleared only by callers giving up at their own dial-tone timeout. The waits of whoever is still waiting get longer; they are served lowest port first.
- Recovery therefore takes about one dt_ms: 3 s at scale 8 (r3 backlog 14/18 cleared by 10-11 s; r5 31/33 cleared in 3 s), about 7 s on the chain without the re-draw, and 15-20 s at real timers (r30 backlog 12→7→4→1→0 at 5 s steps).
- Once cleared, dial tone is back to normal (dt 5-400 ms).

Fairness: the priority is fixed, lowest port first.
- r3 (4x): block 2x NODT 5%, 5x and 7x 100%.
- r5 (10x): 2x 21%, 4x-7x 92-100%.
- R1: 2x 65%, 3x-7x 78-97%.
- r30 at real timers: 2x and 3x 0%, 4x 12%, 5x 43%, 6x 80%, 7x 83%.

Local service while the network side is jammed (24 of 48 lines retrying network calls): see the network-jam-denies-local-service finding.

Bursts (r6: all 96 phones lift in one ms): per burst, 13 of 96 are served within 3 s (one every ~0.46 s per exchange) and 86% get NODT. Of the 26 served over both bursts, 12 found the called line off hook (BUSY), 11 were refused and 3 connected. The unit reading 48 lifted lines at once caused nothing.

Abandonment storms (r7, r8a, r8b): 78 abandons at every phase, and r12 added 15 hang-ups 100 ms after a lone key.
- Phases covered: before the key; 20-47 ms after the key, inside the hunt and seize window; during e and b; around b and the claim; during h s; after the last digit and during ringing.
- Result: no port, register or unit leak, and every invariant passes.

Pathological patterns (resource hold timed from the key to the tone):
| pattern | run | outcome | hold |
|---|---|---|---|
| hot spot | r9 | all 10 network claims refused by the hot line's own exchange | - |
| bad code | r10 | N_TCLAIM, heard mid-dial | 634 ms |
| 1 8 x (reserved) | r14 | N_SVC at e | 272 ms |
| 1 e and stop | r13a | N_TKEY | 655 ms |
| 1 e b of a real code and stop | r13b | N_NODIG only | 1554 ms; ~13 s of register at real timers |
| own code | r13c | local_go, 7 of 13 OK | - |

All of these are bounded.
cluster_sightings:
C15:
- Seen in every run with network traffic: 298 claims, 15 taken, 283 refused (95%). In the overload runs alone, 213 of 228 claims were refused (93%).
- att_take is 0-4 per run. It is 0 in R1, r7, r9, r12, r16a, r20, r21 and r22, and 2/14 at real timers (r30).
- Mutual refusal was caught live in the r5 recovery phase: A64 and B34, dial tone 160 ms apart, both F_REFUSE.
- The refusal is heard only at o_last, or at NODIG when the caller stops after b (r13b, 6 of 6).
- The hot spot refuses every network caller (r9, 0/10).
- It dominates at 0.7x already (smoke 7/15 refused) and at real timers.

C14:
- Leaf sweeps: every incoming seizure at a leaf runs a sweep that finds nothing (nofwd_empty = seized_in in every tb_load2 run, e.g. r3 12+12, r5 13+13).
- C leaf, r21: nofwd_busy 1 (its own sweep, harmless).
- NMON exhaustion 0 (nomon 0 in all 23 runs). Transit forwarder-busy 0. Resolver exhaustion 0 (B res_max 2 of 2 at 4x, 10x and always-trying).
- The doomed-floods-hold-longest feedback predicted for transits does NOT appear on the chain, because one register an exchange caps the pending floods. The feedback is in the registers instead (C15).

C17: 0. ports_idle PASSed in all 23 runs and no STUCK what=port was seen. This holds across 78 random-moment abandons and 15 hang-ups right after the key, including 6 N_TKEY, 14 N_SVC, 33 N_TCLAIM (r10, r16b) and 6 N_NODIG endings.

C01, C02, C03, C04, C05, C06, C08, C09, C10, C11, C13, C16 and C18: no symptom at any load.
- 0 WRONG, JOINED, XTALK, PHANTOM, IDLEHEAR or DRAINRING (1 WRONGRING and 1 alert_nobell, both one harness artefact in r8a).
- n_glare 0 and unhold 0 in every run; no stuck monitor, resolver, att or hunt.
- Scale-8 T_ARM is 2 ms and the topologies use e = 2 everywhere, so the digit-shift wrong-number clusters (C03, C05, C06) had no matching code to land on. The absence is weak evidence for them.

C07, C12, C19 and C20: not exercised (no link faults, carriers or rings in these topologies).

findings.title: Under overload the one register spends 64-96% of its time on network attempts that are refused; network completion is ~0 above ~1.5x the knee and total completions fall past ~4x
findings.mechanism: rtl/mini_marker.v:282: a claim is refused whenever r_busy is set (outside S_WATCH). rtl/mini_marker.v:496-523 (S_YIELD) keeps the ORIGIN register until u_done, u_nogo, r_gone or r_nodig. rtl/net_unit.v:881 moves N_WAITCL to N_DONE only at o_last (net_unit.v:410, the caller's s), even when the far register has already refused at b. So a refused attempt costs its origin register the full 1 e b h s, twice a local call. Two registers that each hold their own outgoing caller refuse each other's claims. As load rises every register's occupancy tends to 1, refusal tends to 1, and every refusal has already been paid for by the other register: positive feedback.
findings.trigger: Two-way network traffic (pnet 500) offered above about 1 attempt/s/exchange at scale 8, or about 0.15-0.3/s at real timers. Runs: r3 (idle 6000), r5 (idle 1500), r20/r21 (chain), r30 (SCALE1, idle 60000).
findings.consequence: Origin-register share spent on refused network attempts (regshare.py): 33% at 0.7x, 77.5% at 4x, 72% at 10x, 96% under a network jam, 64% at real timers (4712 ms each against 2214 ms for a local call). Network OK: 7/14 at 0.7x, 4/20 at 1.6x, 0/36 at 4x, 0/50 at 10x; on the chain 0/61 at 4x and 0/137 at 10x. Connects/s for the pair: 1.21 (0.7x), 0.78 (1.6x), 1.17 (4x), 0.67 (10x), 0 (always-trying). No safety or liveness failure.
findings.realistic: Yes, at real timers (r30: 2 of 14 claims taken; 64% of register time on refused attempts at 4.7 s each). The real knee is about 11-23 attempts per line per hour on a 48-line exchange. That is above an ordinary busy hour, but refusals are already 25-50% at busy hour (C15), and any redial storm crosses the knee.
findings.evidence: work/load/overload/r3_l2_i6k_step.log: SUMMARY unit att_take=1 att_refuse=11 (A), =1/=10 (B); regshare 'N-NOGO n=12 share=77.5% mean_hold=750'. r5_l2_step.log: att_take 1/13 each; PROG 'ok=0' for 3-6 s. r30_l2s1_step.log: 'hold NOGO N n=12 ... key->tone mean=4185'; att_take=1 att_refuse=4 (A), 1/8 (B). r21_l3_i1500_step.log: att_take=0 at A, B and C. Model: overload/model.py (validated against smoke, R1 and R2).
findings.fix: C15 fix 1: go to N_DONE on 'claimed && dmo==0' (net_unit.v:881) and drop o_last. This saves gates, frees the origin register at b and puts the far refusal on the caller at b; the model gives about a 2x later collapse. Structural options: a register pool (the maximal build: one register card and one origin bank each), or the monitor cell collecting h s so no far register is needed at claim time (cap2 model far_noreg: no collapse). Crude overload control: a 2-3 bit counter of consecutive refused claims that makes the marker refuse the key for a while (about one package).

findings.title: A saturated network side takes the only register away from local callers: lines numbered above the network callers get no dial tone at all; lines below get it 5.7x slower and half their calls are BUSY
findings.mechanism: There is one register: rtl/mini_marker.v:337 takes a caller only with !r_busy. A network caller holds it from dial tone to N_DONE or nogo (see the previous finding: rtl/mini_marker.v:496-523, rtl/net_unit.v:881-882), about 0.73 s at scale 8 and 4.7 s real. Register frees are tick-aligned (rtl/pulse_rx.v:77-99, rtl/pulse_reg.v:161; tick_1k = scan 00 at rtl/mini_marker.v:150), so the next caller taken is the lowest-numbered waiting line. Retrying network callers in lower ports win the register every time. Wherever they sit, each of their attempts is doomed (C15) and costs 2x a local call; the lines they call are off hook waiting, so they are BUSY.
findings.trigger: r16a: on each exchange, lines 20-47 keep retrying network calls (+netlines=24 +netidle_ms=300 +pnet=1000) while lines 50-77 make local calls at idle 20 s. r16b: the same with a nonexistent code. r16e: the classes swapped (+net_hi=1). r16c: baseline with lines 20-47 idle.
findings.consequence: r16a: local-only lines got dial tone for 0 of 16 attempts (10 NODT at 3 s, 6 still waiting at the end); network OK 0/21 (every claim refused); carried 0 E; register occupancy .996. r16b (bad codes): local 0/8 served. r16e (local lines favoured by port): all 13 served, but dial tone 467 ms mean (p90 598) against 82 ms (p90 245) in the r16c baseline, and OK 54% against 91% (6 BUSY: the called network callers were off hook). This contradicts C15's expectation that 'local calls still queue'.
findings.realistic: The cost is proportional to the timers (4.7 s of register per doomed attempt at real timers, r30), so it holds at real timing. It needs a sustained group of callers redialling a failing network destination, e.g. a far exchange whose register is always busy (C15), or one down with its code still dialled. Roughly a quarter of the lines retrying is enough.
findings.evidence: work/load/overload/r16a_l2_jam_net.log: every 'CALL ... kind=L' shows out=NODT dt=- or CUT ab=WAITDT; SUMMARY exchange reg_occ=0.996 origin_occ=0.855; att_take=0 att_refuse=11. r16c_l2_jam_none.log: 'dialtone_delay n=14 mean=84.6'. r16e_l2_jam_net_hi.log: jam.py 'net-lines(20-47) kind=L att=13 served=13 NODT=0% dt_mean=467 OK=54%'. Scripts: overload/jam.py, overload/regshare.py.
findings.fix: Reduce the cost of doomed attempts (C15 fix 1 frees the origin register at b, about half the hold). Limit how much of the register(s) network originations may take: in a pool, a class limit of k registers for flood_go; in the mini marker, refuse the key while recent claims were all refused (a small counter). Serving order by arrival rather than port (next finding) would turn denial into delay. The cost is one counter and a gate, or a register card.

findings.title: Waiting callers are served lowest port first, because almost every register release happens at tick_1k (scan 00); under sustained overload blocks 5x-7x get almost no dial tone, at both scales
findings.mechanism: tick_1k is frame_stb && scan==00 (rtl/mini_marker.v:150, rtl/net_unit.v:159). pulse_rx decides digits, CLR and settled on it (rtl/pulse_rx.v:77-99; rtl/pulse_reg.v:99 and :161). So the three common releases all happen just after scan 00: S_WATCH's r_settled (rtl/mini_marker.v:550-552), N_DONE at o_last (rtl/net_unit.v:881, 818-822; mini_marker.v:511), and the T_KEY/T_CLAIM nogos (net_unit.v:876-882, tmr counted on the tick). S_IDLE then takes the first fresh M and not-BUSY port (rtl/mini_marker.v:337), which is the lowest-numbered waiting line. Only a BUSY or NOGO decided at the called port's turn (S_PROBE) restarts the search from that port.
findings.trigger: Any backlog of waiting lines: r3, r5, R1, r21, r30 (real timers), r6 (burst).
findings.consequence: NODT share by port block: r3 (4x) 2x 5%, 3x 42%, 4x 75%, 5x 100%, 6x 84%, 7x 100%. r5 (10x) 2x 21% up to 7x 100%. r21 (chain 10x) 2x 25/38 served, other blocks 2-4 of about 40. r30 (real timers) 2x 0%, 3x 0%, 4x 12%, 5x 43%, 6x 80%, 7x 83%. Arrival order is inverted: in r3 A35 got dial tone before A70, which had lifted 570 ms earlier, and B's backlog was served 31, 33, 34, 40 (waited 2819 ms), 60 (waited 2988 ms, just under NODT).
findings.realistic: Yes at real timers (r30). It matters only under congestion. Known and accepted: memory note mini-marker-jams (Joel, 2026-09-25: 'we might WANT priority', extensions.md 2.4.1 P/PWAIT, do not build round-robin). The new facts are that the priority is by port number, via the tick-aligned release, and how large it is.
findings.evidence: work/load/overload/fair.py over r3_l2_i6k_step.log, r5_l2_step.log, r1_l2_always.log, r21_l3_i1500_step.log, r30_l2s1_step.log (tables in overload/NOTES.md). r3_l2_i6k_step.log CALL ids 98, 99, 100, 95, 96 (B31..B60, dt 9292..10676).

findings.title: After overload the exchange recovers in one dial-tone timeout: nothing is latched, but the backlog is cleared only by waiting callers giving up
findings.mechanism: There is no queue and no overload state: rtl/mini_marker.v:337 serves one waiting line per register hold (0.35-0.75 s scale 8, 2.2-4.7 s real), lowest port first. Lines it cannot reach wait off hook until their own timeout. PROG shows the monitors and resolvers idle at the next sample.
findings.trigger: A load step from overload to below the knee: r3 (4x to 0.7x at 8 s), r5 (10x to 0.7x at 6 s), r21 (chain 10x to 0.7x), r30 (SCALE1, idle 60 s to 400 s at 30 s). All used +switch_redraw=1 except r21.
findings.consequence: Waiting lines at the step, then how they drained: r3 A 14 / B 18, gone by about 10-11 s; r5 31/33 then 23/20, 9/12, 1/0 at 1 s steps; r21 registers 100% busy until about 13 s, 7 s after the step (lines drawn before it kept lifting); r30 12 then 7, 4, 1, 0 at 5 s steps, about 20 s, with dial tone 1.1-1.4 s mean afterwards. Refusal of network calls goes back to its normal-load level (about 50%), which is itself C15.
findings.realistic: At real timers recovery equals the subscribers' patience: 20 s in the harness (r30). No hysteresis and no stuck state was seen in any run.
findings.evidence: work/load/overload/r5_l2_step.log PROG 'now A:wdt=31 ... B:wdt=33' at t=6000, then wdt=23/20, 9/12, 1/0; r30_l2s1_step.log PROG wdt=12, 7, 4, 1, 0 at t=30000-50000; r3_l2_i6k_step.log 'SWITCH t=8021 redrawn=53'.
findings.fix: None needed. The original harness's +switch_ms leaves idle draws made at the old mean pending, which hides recovery (r21); the overload harness copy's +switch_redraw=1 re-draws them.

findings.title: A caller who stops after 1 e b of a real code holds the origin register and a trunk until the register's NODIG (10 s real): the far refusal is not heard before o_last
findings.mechanism: The far marker's refusal writes 03 with BSY and CLM on the claimed trunk (rtl/mini_marker.v:320-327). The origin connects its caller to that trunk only at N_DONE, which needs o_last (rtl/net_unit.v:881, 818-822, 410). With no h s, the origin ends only on the register's no-digit timer (rtl/pulse_reg.v:161-164, then net_unit.v:413 o_gone and mini_marker.v:515 r_nodig).
findings.trigger: r13b: network callers dial 1 2 3 (B's real code) and stop, at idle 6000.
findings.consequence: All 6 ended NOGO why=N_NODIG, heard 1270 ms after b (1554 ms after the key); reg_maxrun 1.6 s at scale 8. At real timers that is about 13 s of the exchange's only register (3.3 s for e b plus 10 s NODIG) and a trunk for an abandoned partial dial.
findings.realistic: Real timers: a caller who pauses or gives up after the code is common (a misremembered number). The cost scales with NODIG.
findings.evidence: work/load/overload/r13b_l2_key_eb.log: 'hold NOGO BAD n=6 ... key->tone mean=1544 ... last->tone mean=1270'; SUMMARY nogo_written N_NODIG=3 F_REFUSE=3 at each exchange; reg_maxrun_ms=1626/1607.
findings.fix: C15 fix 1 (N_DONE at the claim) connects the caller at b, so the refusal is heard at once and the origin register is freed.

findings.title: Doomed floods (bad code, reserved digit, lone key, key and e) are all bounded under load, and C14's transit feedback does not occur on a chain where each exchange has one register
findings.mechanism: One origin bank per exchange (rtl/net_unit.v:842, N_IDLE on flood_go) means at most one flood per neighbour is pending at a transit, so NRES = NMON = 2 suffice on a chain. Doomed floods end at T_CLAIM (net_unit.v:882), the reserved-digit check (:865, isvc at :170) or T_KEY (:876). Every incoming seizure at a leaf still sweeps for nothing (C14 leaf sweeps).
findings.trigger: r10 (bad code at 4x), r14 (1 8 3 h s), r12/r13a (key only; 1 e), r16b (bad-code jam), r20/r21/r22 (chain at 4x, 10x and always-trying).
findings.consequence: Key-to-tone hold: bad code 634 ms (heard before s in 10 of 11 at scale 8, and also before s at real timers, where T_CLAIM 2 s is less than about 2.6 s of h s); reserved digit 272 ms (N_SVC at e); 1 e 655 ms (N_TKEY). Transit B on the chain at 10x: res_max 2, res_mean .50, nomon 0, nofwd 0. The only nofwd_busy (1, at leaf C in r21) is a leaf's own sweep. The positive feedback C14 predicts appears in the registers instead (first finding).
findings.realistic: Yes. A hub, or a ring with more than one register per exchange (the maximal build), would bring C14 back; see the hub and transit studies.
findings.evidence: work/load/overload/r10_l2_bad.log 'hold NOGO BAD ... key->tone mean=634'; r14_l2_resv8.log 'why N_SVC=14 ... key->tone mean=272'; r13a_l2_key_e.log 'N_TKEY ... key->tone 655'; r21_l3_i1500_step.log 'SUMMARY exchange ex=B ... res_max=2' and 'unit ex=B ... nofwd_busy=0 nomon=0'.
findings.fix: None needed at this size. Stuffing and fixes as in C14 before the maximal build or a hub.

findings.title: Load-harness artefacts that look like faults under overload or unusual dialling: the marker_state watchdog, WRONGRING on a same-ms abandon, DTAGAIN on a one-digit dial, unattributed refusals counted as BUSY, and no re-draw at a load step

(d) :832-834 classifies a NOGO with no attributed reason as BUSY when the called phone was busy, and an unattributed F_REFUSE (:1381) falls through to that.

findings.title: A hot line's own exchange, its register busy telling local callers BUSY, refuses every network caller for that line, even at moments the line is free

capacity:
The star's capacity is limited by the single register at each leaf (C15), not by the hub. Hub resources are sized to that limit.

**Measured goodput curve** (scale 8; 3 leaves of 48 lines; every call leaf to leaf through H):
- 2.0 attempts/s offered: 0.94 completed calls/s (la: 15 of 32). Registers 0.46-0.71 busy. Failures: 10 of 12 far-register refusals, 2 at the hub.
- 6.3 attempts/s: 0.42 completed/s (lb: 5 of 76). Registers 0.85-0.99.
- 21 attempts/s: 0 completed (lc: 0 of 212).

**Conversion to real time.** Divide scale-8 call rates by about 7.2: the register hold is dominated by the gap between digits, 100 ms at scale 8 and 720 ms real.
- la's 2.0/s is about 0.28/s real, or about 330 network calls an hour per leaf. That is about 7.7 times network.md 5's design of 43 network calls an hour per leaf.
- The measured holds scale as expected. A resolver is held 262 ms (scale 8) against 1838 ms (real) from forward to claim, a ratio of 7.0. A doomed flood holds it 624 ms against 4486 ms, which is 2.4 times a claimed flood's hold at both scales.

**Register arithmetic at real timers.**
- A network call costs about 5.0 register-seconds at the origin (dial tone to N_DONE) and about 2.5 at the destination (claim to s). A local call costs about 2.3.
- At the design load (per leaf: 101 local calls an hour, 43 network out, 43 network in) that is about 555 s an hour. Register occupancy is about 0.15, so about 15% of claims are refused (C15's figure).
- The goodput peak falls between la and lb. At real timers that is roughly 0.04-0.1 completed network calls/s per leaf.

**Hub resources.**
- One origin bank and one register per leaf means at most one flood per leaf is pending at the hub. With NRES=2 at a 3-leaf hub, the loss is the chance that all three leaves have a flood pending at once. That is about 5e-4 at the design load.
- Measured share of hub floods lost this way: la 1 of 30, lb 2 of 45, lc 11 of 42 (26%), le 11 of 49. With NRES=3 it was 0 of 44 (res_max reached 3).
- **Sizing rule:** NRES equal to the number of leaves (registers beyond the hub) removes the loss: 3 here, 4 at a full four-direction hub.
- NMON=2 at the hub is shared by every flood in the network, because each flood holds a hub cell until its e digit is decided (about 0.9 s real). Calls to the hub fail when two other floods are in that window: reproduced in r3. At the design load this is about 5e-4.
- NMON=2 at a leaf is enough while the hub is silent (at most two flood sources). With the hub also originating there are three sources, and 2 calls in le were lost to NOMON at the called leaf.

**Forwarder.**
- Forwarder-busy losses (la 1, lb 4, lc 3, bb 2) occur only at scale 8.
- At real timers the C_HOLD watch spaces classifications 19.25 ms apart, and the forward takes 10.6 ms (s1_burst).

**Links.**
- 8-channel spokes never had more than 5 of 8 busy in any run; the registers throttle first.
- With 2-channel spokes, floods alone fill the links. A flood holds a channel on every spoke until its claim, so a spoke can carry its own leaf's flood plus one leg for every other leaf's flood.
- Result on 2-channel spokes (bb): 29 of 81 attempts had no free trunk (N_NOTRUNK), and 20 of 34 hub forwards reached only one of the two other leaves.
- **Spoke sizing rule:** channels ≥ talking calls + number of leaves.

**Statistical weight.** 888 attempts over 212 simulated seconds (28,758 wall seconds). The load points are single seeds of 32-212 attempts. Rates below about 10% are ±50% or worse.
overload:
**Goodput collapses to zero past register saturation, and the collapse persists after the load drops.**

**lc (about 21 attempts/s offered):**
- 0 of 212 attempts completed; carried 0.000 E.
- 119 attempts got no dial tone within 3 s; 49 were still waiting at the hang-up.
- Every claim was refused: att_take 0, att_refuse 28 at the leaves.
- Dial-tone delay averaged 988 ms, with a 99th percentile of 3 s.
- The hub lost 26% of floods to BUSY-NORES and 7% to BUSY-FWDR (the latter only at scale 8). Links stayed at 2 of 8 busy.

**Mechanism.**
- A claim is refused the instant it finds the register busy (mini_marker.v:282).
- A freed register is given to the next off-hook line within one scan pass (mini_marker.v:330-352).
- So a claim succeeds only if it arrives in about 1 ms per register cycle (about 0.8 s at scale 8, 6-7 s real).
- This does not depend on the timer scale, so it holds at real timers too. That is argued, not simulated at SCALE1.

**Load step (lstep):**
- Overload for 5 s, then 1.2 attempts/s, which is below la's 2.0/s where 0.94 calls/s completed.
- No call completed in the whole 15 s.
- Registers stayed 100% busy for about 9 s after the step, while the backlog of lines already off hook drained. They fell to 0.52 only in the last interval.
- The collapse is metastable: a burst of about 36 s real would leave about a minute of zero goodput after the load drops.

**It degrades without damage.**
- There were no wrong numbers, no joins and no phantom rings in the 212-, 189- and 88-attempt overload runs.
- Every drain ended with all 50 invariants passing: ports, registers, markers, origins, monitors, resolvers, sweeps and queues idle, and links up.
- The only STUCK lines are the harness's marker_state watchdog, which samples at 1 kHz while the marker cycles DRAIN, IDLE, READ inside one millisecond. The register watchdog never fired.

**Hub under overload.** Resolvers and cells saturate; three flood sources exceed NRES=2 in 22-26% of floods. The hub never wedges: every resolver was freed by R_LEG, R_GONE or a claim at the hub.

**Unstrapped ring** (g3, about 3.8 attempts/s):
- Lap copies nearly double the hub's seizures (79 against 42).
- They exhaust monitors (28 with none at A) and resolvers (43 floods not forwarded at A).
- Carried traffic falls from 0.47 E with the straps to 0.11 E. No wrong numbers.

findings.title: Past register saturation the network's goodput falls to zero and stays there while a dial-tone backlog exists: every claim is refused because a freed register is re-taken by a waiting caller within a millisecond
findings.mechanism: rtl/mini_marker.v:282: att_refuse = u_att && r_busy (except S_WATCH), so a claim that finds the register busy is refused at once. rtl/mini_marker.v:320-328 then writes 03 with CLAIM on the trunk. rtl/mini_marker.v:273-274: att_take needs !r_busy. S_IDLE (rtl/mini_marker.v:330-352) gives a freed register to the next off-hook line within one scan pass. rtl/net_unit.v:656-676 writes CLAIM before asking for the register, and the origin takes the refused claim as its claim (rtl/net_unit.v:795-804, 881). When every call is a network call, a completion needs the far leaf's register to be free at the instant of the claim. At saturation that window is about 1 ms per register cycle.
findings.trigger: tb_hub star, 3 leaves of 48 lines, all traffic leaf to leaf (+pnet=1000 +orig_x=14 +net_to=14). lc_idle5: idle 5 s, about 21 attempts/s. lstep_5to120: 5 s of that, then idle 120 s.
findings.consequence: Goodput curve: 2.0 attempts/s gives 0.94 completed/s; 6.3/s gives 0.42/s; 21/s gives 0. Carried 0.000 E, 119 of 212 attempts got no dial tone, and every claim was refused. After the offered load dropped to 1.2/s, below the knee, registers stayed 100% busy for about 9 s and no call completed in the remaining 10 s: the collapse is metastable. No stuck state, no wrong number.
findings.realistic: Yes. The refusal is instantaneous and the free window is one scan pass at both scales, so this holds at real timers. That is argued; no overload run was made at SCALE1. The knee moves to about 1/7 of the scale-8 rate: roughly 0.1 network attempts/s per leaf, several times network.md 5's design load. At the design load (register occupancy about 0.15) it does not occur. It is C15's overload behaviour; C15 calls the loss graceful and it is not.

findings.fix: (a) The only full fix: a second register on the mini marker reserved for claims, so a claim never competes with a new caller. Cost: one more register's digit store and counters (the register's package count, roughly 6-10 packages) plus an arbitration gate. (b) Cheaper and partial: a 'claim imminent' line from the unit (any cell in M_WANT_B) that stops S_IDLE (rtl/mini_marker.v:337) handing a freed register to a new caller, plus a bounded wait on att (up to about 500 ms real, less than the far caller's gap between digits). This needs one ribbon line and a few gates. It only helps when the register frees between the far caller's e and b, so it shrinks the collapse without removing it. (c) C15's connect-at-claim roughly halves the origin register's hold and moves the knee about 2x.

findings.title: A hub of single-register leaves never needs more resolvers than it has leaves; NRES=2 at a 3-leaf hub silently drops the third concurrent flood, and NRES=3 removes the loss
findings.mechanism: rtl/net_unit.v:616-621: forward only if fst==F_IDLE && rs_free_any; otherwise the seizure is held and counted in nf_busy (506-507). Each forward takes a resolver (737-741), freed only by R_LEG, R_GONE (681-708) or a local claim (659-665). One origin bank per unit (nst, 384-400) and one register per mini marker mean each leaf has at most one flood pending at the hub. After a drop, R_GONE frees the resolver T_REL+1 ms later, before the leaf's next key can arrive (at least 110 ms at scale 8, 730 ms real). So the peak demand equals the number of leaves.
findings.trigger: r2_three: three leaves key within 120 ms; the third flood at A shows 'mon=0 fwd=BUSY-NORES'. s1_burst: the same at real timers. Under load: la, lb, lc, lstep, le.
findings.consequence: The third flood is held at the hub listening to 00 and never reaches its owner. The caller waits T_CLAIM and gets NOGO N_TCLAIM (2 s after b at real timers). Share of hub floods lost: la 3%, lb 4%, lc 26%, lstep 27%, le 22%. With NRES=3, 0 of 44 (res_max 3). **Benches**
- `tb_hub.sv` is the star: hub A, code 1 1; leaves B 2 2, C 2 3, D 2 4. H faces N via block 1 to B, E via block 3 to C, S via block 5 to D. Each leaf's block 1 faces the hub with g.

  - `+define+HUB_STRAP` adds STRAP_N on that link at both ends.
- `tb_hubb.sv` is the same star on baseband ties, 2 channels per spoke.
- Both carry HUB instrumentation lines (SEIZE by=, FWD, RES LEG/GONE with claim hops or NOCLAIM, CLAIM HERE/LATE, OCLAIM hops or SUSPECT) and a HUBSUM line at the end.
- `load_harness.svh` is a copy of the shared harness plus `+net_to=MASK` (the exchanges a network call may dial).
- Tools: `parse.py` (summary), `attrib.py` (follows each call through the hub), `resocc.py` (hub resolver occupancy), `table.py` (per-run table).
- Builds are binary-only (1.4 MB each): `obj_hub` (scale 8), `obj_hub_s1` (SCALE1), `obj_hub_r3` (NRES=3), `obj_ring`, `obj_ringst`, `obj_hubb`.
- The queue runner is `job1.sh` plus `q/*.sh` and `lib.sh`; results are in `runs.rc`.

**Directed answers**
- Leaf to leaf through H: A forwards 10.6 ms after classifying, with 2 legs. The owner claims at b's ID. A's resolver sees the leg's M within 1 ms, points the in-port at it and drops the other leg. The origin sees the claim about 2 ms later.
- A call to H: H's cell claims and frees the resolver (HERE).
- Bad code: both legs are counted to b and dropped. The resolver is freed by R_GONE at T_CLAIM + T_REL.
- Hang-up during the fan-out: R_GONE frees the resolver at hang-up + T_REL, 5 times out of 5.
- Two fan-outs at once: fine.
- A third fan-out: not forwarded at all, and also unwatched at H. So the RTL does not patch into the first direction as network.md says.

**Real-timer re-checks (SCALE1)**
- The basic paths and the burst were re-run at real timers.
- The forwarder-busy loss disappears at real timers; the resolver and monitor losses remain.
- The overload collapse was argued to be timer-independent but not simulated at SCALE1: a SCALE1 overload run would take hours of wall time.

**Not done**
- The bad-code-only resolver stress (staged, not run).
- Link outages.
- More seeds per load point.

**Safety over all 19 runs (888 attempts)**
- 0 wrong numbers, 0 phantom rings, 0 WRONGRING, 0 crosstalk.
- 1 joined pair (the C13 leg glare on 2-channel spokes).
- All 50 invariants passed after every drain.
- The only STUCK lines are the marker_state watchdog artefact.
