- B's register: 0 in mix (a); 0.59 uniform heavy; 0.86-0.97 at overload; 0.90 in the B-originated mix.
- Links: busy mean 0.8-3.2 channels of 8, max 7 (A-B, T6). Never full: no N_NOTRUNK, no glare.

Why the resolvers never run out: each exchange has one register and one origin bank. So at most one flood from A and one from C can be waiting for a claim at B. That is k = 2 sources for NRES = 2.

With NRES = 1 (T8), B lost 8 of 35 floods (22.9 %). Engset with k = 2, n = 1 and p = 0.85/s x 0.26 s = 0.22 predicts 22 %. So the model is checked.

Extrapolation (arithmetic, not run; Engset, real timers):
- Per-source pending fraction p = 0.44 x u, where u is the source register's occupancy by network calls that cross the transit. The 0.44 is resolver hold 1.8-2.5 s over register time 4.4-6.4 s per network attempt, both measured in T9 and T10.
- NRES = 2, 3 sources (inner transit of a 4-chain): 1.2 % at u = 0.25, 4.8 % at 0.5, 19 % saturated.
- NRES = 2, 4 sources: 3.2 / 11 / 36 %. 8 sources: 15 / 36 / 67 %.
- NRES = 3, 4 sources: 0.1 / 1.1 / 8.5 %.
- network.md §10's Erlang-B 1.4 % is the wrong model for a transit fed by single-register exchanges.

The chain's real limit is the one register per exchange, and C15:
- Register time per network attempt, including incoming h s: about 0.87 s at scale 8 and 6.4 s at real timers. A register saturates at about 1 attempt/s at scale 8, which is about 0.13-0.16/s or 480-560 network attempts an hour at real timers.
- Share of all calls (every one of them a network call) refused by the far register: 19 % at register occupancy 0.47 (T2, 4 of 21), 49 % at 0.75 (T3, 18 of 37), 100 % for crossings (T4, T9).
- Completed network calls for the whole chain peak at 0.65-0.73/s at scale 8 (T1-T3). That is about 0.09/s, or 320 an hour, at real timers.
- B-originated calls to idle far registers reach 1.05/s (T5).

Scale 8 to real time: divide rates by about 8. Holds scale about 7.0x (res_hold 261 ms becomes 1833 ms).
overload:
Past register saturation the chain collapses; it does not level off. The cause is C15.
- T6 (2.2 attempts/s at A and C, registers 0.86-0.995): 67 of 72 claims refused; 5 of 119 network calls completed.
- T7 (3.1-3.5 attempts/s, registers 0.96-0.996): 61 of 65 refused; 3 of 139 network calls completed. Local calls still complete (32).
- Completed network calls per second: 0.65-0.73 at heavy load, 0.25 in T6, 0.14 in T7.
- Dial tone delay: mean 0.69-0.82 s, p99 2.9 s at scale 8 (about 23 s real). NODT 24-48 %.

The feedback loop:
- A doomed call keeps its origin register for the whole dial. A refusal is heard only when the origin connects after h s (mini_marker.v:320-327 with net_unit.v:881).
- A flood lost at the transit is heard only at T_CLAIM after b (net_unit.v:882).
- So refused calls keep every register saturated, and that makes the next claims fail too.

B under overload holds up: it forwarded 49 of 51 and 41 of 43 floods. The only losses were 2 + 2 FWDBUSY of the scale-8 kind. RESNONE 0, no glare, no leg glare, no stuck resolver or monitor, links at most 7/8.

Safety and liveness hold at every load:
- 0 wrong numbers, joined, phantom rings, cross-talk, wrong rings or idle-hear in all 13 runs.
- Every run drains to 38/38 invariants (2.5 s at scale 8, 10 s real). Recovery is immediate once the load goes.
- The only STUCK lines were the harness's marker_state watchdog firing on continuous service (T6 18.2 s, T7 22.0 s). The register watchdog never fired. This is a bench gap, not a hang.
- Caveat: T7's +switch_ms step is soft. Phones scheduled before the switch keep their 8 s mean idle, so offered load decays over about 10 s. Recovery during traffic is not shown; the drain is.
cluster_sightings:
C14 (forward resources):
- Forwarder busy (FWDBUSY) at scale 8:
  - Random traffic: T1 0/23, T2 0/21, T3 2/34, T6 2/51, T7 2/43, T8 1/35. Total 7/207, 3.4 % of floods. In every case the forwarder was in F_HUNT for the other flood and both resolvers were free (rsb=00).
  - Crossings (T4): 10 of 15 lost, which is every crossing whose upstream writes were at most 8.1 ms apart.
- Real timers (T9, T10): 0 of 27, including 6 crossings 1.1-8.6 ms apart, each classified after the 18.6-19.4 ms watch and forwarded.
- RESNONE: 0 of 293 with NRES=2; 8 of 35 with NRES=1.
- Leaf sweeps for nothing: every incoming flood at A and C (nofwd_empty = seized_in in every run, e.g. T6 A 49/49). One leaf FWDBUSY (T1 A).
- Lost-forward cost (20 cases): origin trunk + B in-port + B monitor held 504-558 ms; caller's cannot-complete 533-588 ms after the key, at or before the end of dialling (8 of 20 before the last digit).
- NMON exhaustion: 0.

C15 (one register), the dominant failure at every load:
- F_REFUSE plus inferred refusals: T1 16/16 NOGO, T2 4/4, T3 18/19, T4 20/30, T9 18/18, T5 1, T6 62, T7 56.
- att_refuse/claims at heavy load: A 11/18, C 8/14. At overload: A 30/32, C 20/20 (T6); A 23/23 (T7).
- Who held the far register, over 175 refusals (refuse.py): its own outgoing network caller alone 126; a local caller 12; another incoming 4; mixed 32.
- The previous call's second party, taken as a caller after the other party cleared: alone once (T5), 8 times mixed.
- Refusal heard 20 ms (scale 8) or 132 ms (real) after the last digit.

C05: classifier serialisation seen at real timers. The second of two floods within 18 ms waits out the watch: hop 18.5-21.3 ms (T9). No flood arrived more than 40 ms after its upstream write. No wrong number.

Not seen in any run, and why:
- C13: 0 (res_leg_noclaim 0, res_leg_glare 0, n_glare 0). Links peaked at 7/8, and glare needs the last free channel.
- C09 and C18: 0 forwards after the incoming was claimed, released or cancelled (fwd_in_dead, fwd_in_claimed, fwd_fcancel all 0). 0 UNHOLDs at B. C09 needs port 77; B's in-ports are 10-17 and 30-37.
- C08 and C10: 0 resolvers never freed (res_held_at_end 0, no resolver or monitor STUCK). No stuck-A or link-cut stimulus was applied.
- C17: no port left BUSY (ports_idle PASS every run).
- C03, C04, C06: 0 UNHOLDs anywhere and no short seizures, so they were not exercised.
- C01, C02, C11, C12, C16, C19, C20: no symptom.

findings.title: The one forwarder loses the second of two crossing floods only at scale 8; at real timers the T_ARM watch spaces them past the forward
findings.mechanism:
- net_unit.v:616-621: a forward starts only if fst==F_IDLE && rs_free_any at the C_ACT write, with no retry. The miss is counted only in n_nofwd (:506-507, :545).
- net_unit.v:714-743: a forward is F_WANT, then the 9 ms sweep and 1 ms confirm, then F_WRITE. Measured 10.6-12.4 ms after classification.
- net_unit.v:283-284 and :584-588: classification happens only in C_IDLE, and C_HOLD watches each hold for T_ARM+2 ticks. That is 4 ms at scale 8 and 18 ms at real timers.
findings.trigger: Two floods reach the transit from opposite sides within about 12 ms, for example A->C and C->A keyed together.
findings.consequence:
At scale 8 the second flood is held and monitored but never forwarded. Its caller gets cannot-complete (N_TCLAIM) at T_CLAIM after b.

At real timers the second flood's classification waits out the watch until 18.6-19.4 ms after the first. By then the first's forward is written, so the second is forwarded, with a hop about 19 ms longer.
findings.realistic:
Survives real timing only as a triple coincidence: B's own origin sweep delays the first forward past the watch (F_WANT waits for hst idle, net_unit.v:715) and a second flood lands in the ~4 ms window after it. Arithmetic: about 1e-6 per flood at real busy-hour rates.

Scale-8 load studies overstate this loss by construction: 7/207 floods (3.4 %) in random traffic and 10/15 crossings at scale 8, against 0/27 at real timers.
findings.evidence:
- t4_cross_s8.log:66 'TP t=135.610 ... ex=B SEIZE p=B37 ... fwd=FWDBUSY fst=2 ... rsb=00'. cross.py: 10/10 crossings with upstream gap 1.3-8.1 ms lost, 5/5 with gap >= 19.5 ms forwarded.
- t9_cross_s1.log:68 't=749.548 ... SEIZE p=B37 ... fwd=yes ... hop=18.47'. 9 crossings with gaps 1.1-26.8 ms, 18/18 forwarded.
- t3_e2e_heavy.log:184/186: C flood classified at 9805.6, A flood at 9812.3 FWDBUSY, forwarder in F_HUNT, both resolvers free.
findings.fix:
Tested pending-forward slot in work/load/transit/fix/net_unit.v:
- It keeps one port, its mask and its age, and starts the forward when the forwarder is idle and a resolver is free.
- It drops the pending forward on UNHOLD of that port, on a claim of it here, when its M is seen low, or at 24 ms.
- Results: t4_cross_s8_fix 10/10 forwarded 13.4-17.7 ms late; t3_e2e_heavy_fix 34/34; 38/38 invariants; no new failures.
- Cost: about 3 packages ('574, '161, a flag and a comparator).

Optional at real timers. Scale-8 benches should discount FWDBUSY.

findings.title: Transit resolver loss is Engset in the number of single-register exchanges whose floods cross it: zero on the 3-chain with NRES=2, 22.9 % with NRES=1; network.md §10's Erlang-B 1.4 % is the wrong model
findings.mechanism:
- net_unit.v:616: forward only with rs_free_any.
- net_unit.v:737-741: a resolver is taken for every forward, including a chain's single leg.
- net_unit.v:659-665 and :681-708: it is freed only at the claim (rs_mine or R_LEG), or at R_GONE after the origin drops.
- One register (mini marker) and one origin bank (net_unit.v:71-73, :842-846): each exchange has at most one flood waiting for a claim.
findings.trigger: Floods from k distinct origin exchanges crossing one transit at once, with k > NRES.
findings.consequence:
Measured:
- 3-chain (k=2): 0 RESNONE in 293 floods with NRES=2, at all loads and at real timers.
- NRES=1 (T8): 8/35 = 22.9 % not forwarded. Engset (k=2, n=1, p=0.22) predicts 22 %.

Extrapolated (arithmetic; p = 0.44 x u, u = register occupancy by network calls crossing the transit):
- NRES=2, 3 sources: 1.2 % at u=0.25, 4.8 % at 0.5, 19 % saturated.
- NRES=2, 4 sources: 3.2 / 11 / 36 %.
- NRES=2, 8 sources: 15 / 36 / 67 %.

Each loss is silent (see lost-forward-cost).
findings.realistic: Survives real timing: the holds are digit times, and the p ratio is scale-invariant. res_hold is 261 ms at scale 8 and 1833-1847 ms at real timers (T9, T10).
findings.evidence:
- NOTES.md summary table: all NRES=2 logs show TPSUM ex=B nofwd_resnone=0, with res_max 2.
- t8_e2e_heavy_nres1.log:100, 235, 252 'fwd=RESNONE ... rsb=1'; TPSUM ex=B seize=35 nofwd_resnone=8.
findings.fix:
- Size NRES at a transit to at least the number of other exchanges whose floods can cross it. With one register each, that makes the loss zero (NRES = n-1 at the inner transits of an n-chain). About 4.5 packages a resolver.
- Or add the documented one-leg fallback.
- Rewrite §10's arithmetic as Engset over sources.

findings.title: A flood the transit does not forward costs about 4.5 s of trunk and caller time at real timers, and nothing but n_nofwd sees it (which also counts every leaf's incoming)
findings.mechanism:
- net_unit.v:609-615: the unforwarded seizure is still held BUSY with a monitor.
- net_unit.v:882: the origin drops only at T_CLAIM after b (N_WAITCL -> N_DROP -> nogo).
- net_unit.v:506-508 and :545: n_nofwd adds nf_busy and nf_empty. nf_empty fires for every incoming flood at a leaf, because fwd_mask includes directions with no trunk.
findings.trigger: Any FWDBUSY or RESNONE at the transit when the owner lies beyond it.
findings.consequence:
Measured over 20 cases at scale 8:
- The origin's A-B channel, B's in-port and a B monitor were held 504-558 ms (a normal flood holds about 290 ms to its claim).
- The caller heard cannot-complete 533-588 ms after the key, at or before the end of the dial (8/20 before the last digit).
- Real-time equivalent: about 4.0-4.5 s and 4.3-4.7 s.

At the leaves nofwd_empty equals seized_in in every run (T6 A 49/49), so n_nofwd is useless as an alarm.
findings.realistic: Real timing: T_CLAIM 2 s after b.
findings.evidence: tr_an.py LOST-FWD lines, for example t8: 'flood A caller=A61 ... why=RESNONE ... origin trunk held 544 ms | ... why=N_TCLAIM key=12349 last=- tone=12923'.
findings.fix:
- The pending forward removes the forwarder case (tested).
- A transit that cannot forward could claim-to-refuse, giving immediate cannot-complete (C14 option).
- Count nofwd only where fwd_mask meets a direction that has a trunk (one AND with the sweep's per-direction found bits).

findings.title: Far-register refusal is the dominant end-to-end failure through the transit at every load, and past saturation it causes congestion collapse
findings.mechanism:
- mini_marker.v:273-282: att_take needs a free register; att_refuse fires whenever r_busy.
- mini_marker.v:320-327: a refusal writes NOGO with CLAIM on the trunk. The caller hears it only when the origin connects at o_last (net_unit.v:881).
- So a doomed call holds its origin register for the whole dial.
findings.trigger: Any claim that finds the far register busy, most often with that exchange's own outgoing network caller. Both ends calling each other always refuse each other.
findings.consequence:
- Medium load (register occupancy 0.47): 19 % of network calls refused (4/21).
- Heavy (0.75): 49 % (18/37). The transit lost only 1-2 floods.
- Crossings: 100 % (T4, T9).
- Overload: 67/72 (T6) and 61/65 (T7) claims refused; 5/119 and 3/139 network calls completed.
- Completed network calls per second fall from 0.65-0.73 to 0.25 and 0.14.
- Who held the far register, over 175 refusals: its own outgoing network caller alone 126, local caller 12, another incoming call 4, mixed 32.
findings.realistic: Survives real timing: T9 refused 18/18 at real timers, with the tone 132 ms after the last digit. It is holding-time arithmetic.
findings.evidence:
- SUMMARY why F_REFUSE and SUMMARY unit att_refuse in every log.
- refuse.py output in work/load/transit/NOTES.md.
- t6_links.log and t7_step.log SUMMARY lines.
findings.fix:
- A register pool, one bank a register (network.md §10).
- Cheaper partials:
  - (a) Hold a refused claim for up to about 0.5 s: the far caller's h is at least 590 ms away, and S_WATCH already waits this way. Cost: a timer.
  - (b) At the claim, write the caller listening to the kept trunk, so a refusal is heard at once and the origin register is freed about 2 s earlier per doomed call. That breaks the collapse feedback. Cost: one write; check it against C12 first.

findings.title: When one party clears, the other (still off hook) is taken as a new caller into its exchange's one register for lag + CLR, and claims arriving then are refused
findings.mechanism:
- port.v:176-194: a port clears on the fall of fE. The callee's port releases when the far caller's M falls through the path.
- mini_marker.v:337: S_IDLE takes any port with M and BUSY clear as a call request. The lingering party is given dial tone and holds the register until its hang-up is timed out (CLR).
findings.trigger: A completed call ends with one party clearing first, and a network claim reaches the other party's exchange within that party's hang-up lag + CLR.
findings.consequence: The claim is refused (C15) although nobody is dialling there. In T5, exchange A had no originating lines, yet the claim 47 ms after the previous call B56->A21 ended was refused.
findings.realistic:
1 clean case (plus 8 mixed) in 175 refusals, with the harness's lag of 50 ms at scale 8 or 400 ms real. With people who wait seconds before hanging up, it holds the register for lag + 0.26 s per call end.

Confidence is 'likely': the mechanism is inferred from timing, not traced.
findings.evidence: t5_borig.log:74 'TP t=1680.001 ... ex=A CLAIM p=A16'; :85 'CALL id=2 from=B67 to=A53 ... out=NOGO why=F_REFUSE'. The previous call id=1 B56->A21 has end=1633.
findings.fix:
- The marker offers dial tone only to a port whose E did not just fall under a standing M: a hold-off of a few hundred ms, like the unit's st bit. Cost: a bit a port or a timer.
- Or a register pool.

findings.title: The harness's marker_state watchdog reports STUCK under saturation while the marker is serving callers back to back
findings.mechanism: load_harness.svh:1445: wd_run(wd_mk[x], ld_mks != 0, 6*NODIG, 'marker_state'). At register saturation the mini marker goes from one caller to the next without an IDLE millisecond sample.
findings.trigger: Register occupancy about 1.0 for more than 7.5 s at scale 8.
findings.consequence:
STUCK marker_state lines appear although A gave dial tone every 0.7-0.8 s:
- T6: from 9381, held 18.2 s.
- T7: from 7527, held 22.0 s.

The register watchdog stayed silent, STUCK-END came at the traffic stop, and invariants were 38/38. The SUMMARY safety 'stuck=1' is not a hang.
findings.realistic: Bench only.
findings.evidence:
- t6_links.log:435 and :889 (STUCK and STUCK-END).
- t7_step.log:365 and :916.
- A's CALL lines show dial tone at 2296, 3038, 3780, 4562, 5304, 6166 ...
findings.fix: In the harness, reset wd_mk on each register attach or dial tone, or watch for no progress rather than 'not IDLE'.

findings.title: Measured transit hop under load: about 13 ms (2.1-2.9 ms to classify, 10.6-10.8 ms to forward); about 19 ms more for the second of two floods at real timers
findings.mechanism:
- net_unit.v:283-292: classification at the port's turn plus the word read.
- net_unit.v:715-743: sweep, confirm pass, write.
- net_unit.v:584-588: the T_ARM watch.
findings.trigger: Every forward.
findings.consequence:
- Classification 2.1-2.9 ms after the upstream write (p99 3.3).
- Forward 10.55-10.78 ms mean after classification. p99 12-18 ms when a classification read or B's own origin sweep interleaves (T6 max 17.7).
- Origin write to the far leaf's classification: about 15 ms.
- At real timers the second flood's hop is 18.5-21.3 ms (T9).
- No flood arrived more than 40 ms after its upstream write.

findings.realistic: Real: measured in T9 and T10.
findings.evidence: TPHIST lines, for example t9_cross_s1.log 'TPHIST ex=B what=hop ... p90=18 ... max=21.34' and 'seize_to_fwd mean=10.67'; t6_links.log 'seize_to_fwd ... p99=17 max=17.74'.
findings.fix: None. This is input for the guard-reach arithmetic.

findings.title: No transit race appeared under load: 0 late forwards, legs onto taken channels, leg glare, stuck resolvers or legs left BUSY in 357 floods into B
findings.mechanism:
The probe's counters (tr_probe_unit.svh), per exchange, over 13 runs:
- fwd_in_dead, fwd_in_claimed, fwd_fcancel: C09/C18.
- fwd_leg_taken.
- res_leg_noclaim and res_leg_glare: C13.
- res_held_at_end: C08/C10.
- unhold, nomon.
- ports_idle invariant.
findings.trigger: All mixes, from medium load to overload, at both scales.
findings.consequence:
All zero. Why:
- C13 needs the last free channel; the links peaked at 7/8.
- C09 needs a seizure dying in the last CONFIRM sample on port 77; B's in-ports are 10-17 and 30-37.
- C08/C10 need a stuck A or a link cut.
- C03/C04 need short seizures; there were no UNHOLDs.
findings.realistic: Arithmetic: leg glare on an 8-channel link at these loads is below 1e-4 per flood.
findings.evidence: TPSUM lines in every log (for example t6_links.log TPSUM ex=B ... fwd_leg_taken=0 res_leg_noclaim=0 res_held_at_end=0). INVARIANT TOTAL pass=38 fail=0 in all 13 runs.
findings.fix: To exercise C13, C09 and C10 under load, a bench needs 1-2 channel links (baseband ties) or a port-77 trunk.
